subject: Tenant provenance & egress assurance — requested topology + evidence
messages:
From: Lina Torres <security-qa@orchidbank.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@orchidbank.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant provenance & egress assurance (follow-up)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Orchid Bank is interested but we need a focused assurance packet for our security review. Specifically we need:

- A network topology showing tenant isolation boundaries for hosted and private deployments (include inter-VPC connectivity and any sidecar/proxy hops).
- Data provenance controls: how we can track which tenant or request caused an outbound flow (audit IDs, correlation fields).
- Egress assurance: examples of allowed egress paths, how egress is prevented from reaching customer-sensitive networks, and controls for third-party destinations.
- Threat-model summary describing how you mitigate lateral movement from an inference node to control plane components.
- Evidence: sample audit logs (recent, masked), and any penetration-testing reports or SOC references you can share.

Can you provide the packet by EOD Friday? If not, please propose a date and a short list of what you can deliver by then.

Best,
Lina
Lina Torres
Senior Security Engineer — Orchid Bank
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Lina Torres <security-qa@orchidbank.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant provenance & egress assurance (follow-up)

Hi Lina —

Thanks for the clear list. We're putting together a concise assurance packet that includes an annotated network diagram, a provenance mapping, egress flow examples, and a short threat-model summary focused on lateral movement and control-plane isolation.

What we can deliver by EOD Friday (2026-10-02):
- Redwood_Tenant_Provenance_Controls.pdf: ~8 pages, with mapping between request IDs, tenant IDs, and audit log fields.
- Redwood_Network_Topology_v2.svg: annotated diagram for Hosted / Dedicated / Private modes.
- audit_log_sample_202609.csv: masked sample showing correlation IDs and egress records.
- egress_flow_examples.txt: three typical allowed/blocked path examples with firewall/filter rules.

If you need penetration test reports or SOC artifacts, those are available under NDA — happy to start the NDA thread separately and share the compressed evidence bundle.

I'll loop in Vanessa and Karthik for technical accuracy on the topology and threat model (cc'd). If Friday is tight we can do an interim delivery by Thursday close-of-business and a follow-up call Friday morning to walk through details.

How does 10:00 AM PT Friday for a 30-min walkthrough sound?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant provenance & egress assurance (follow-up)

Irene / Karthik — quick internal notes before we finalize the packet: 

- Network diagram: annotate the three logical planes we use: inference data plane (tenant workloads), control plane (orchestration, model catalog), and management plane (admin/API). Show explicit egress gate (egress proxy) for Hosted and Dedicated; Private mode shows optional customer-managed NAT/GW.
- Provenance: add the flow example where a single API request carries a X-Request-ID, tenant_id, model_version; explain how these map to our KV cache logs + tokenized audit entries.
- Lateral movement mitigation: highlight process isolation within the runtime (per-workload cgroups), kernel-level seccomp filters for sidecars, and strict mutual TLS between inference nodes and control plane services.
- Egress controls: include both allowlist and per-tenant policy enforcement; show an example policy that prevents outbound connections except to: customer-provided S3 endpoints, Redwood artifact registries, and telemetry sinks under our allowlist.

I'll add a short appendix describing shipper retention windows and how audit logs are hashed and salted before export (that helps them verify provenance without leaking raw data).

Irene — I'll produce a 1-page threat-model summary you can insert into the PDF. Karthik, please confirm the exact header names for the correlation IDs we log.

-Vanessa
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Lina Torres <security-qa@orchidbank.com>, procurement@orchidbank.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final assurance packet: tenant provenance & egress (attached)

Hi Lina —

Per our commitment, attached is the assurance packet for Orchid Bank. Executive summary (key points):

- Tenant boundaries: Logical separation is enforced via per-tenant namespaces in the serving runtime, container-level isolation, and network-level tenant segmentation. Hosted tier uses strict multi-tenant namespaces with enforced inter-tenant ACLs; Dedicated and Private provide physical/virtual isolation options per contract.
- Provenance & correlation: Every inbound request is stamped with a globally unique redwood_request_id and tenant_id at the API gateway. These values are propagated through the runtime and appear in KV-cache logs, egress records, and audit events. audit_log_sample_202609.csv demonstrates the fields: timestamp, redwood_request_id, tenant_id, model_version, egress_host, action.
- Egress controls: Outbound traffic from inference nodes traverses an egress proxy that enforces per-tenant allowlists and DNS filtering. For Hosted/Dedicated we operate the proxy; for Private we provide the configuration and optional sidecar that integrates with customer NAT. Examples in egress_flow_examples.txt illustrate blocked attempts (internal -> external) and allowed S3 sink flows with signed URLs.
- Lateral movement mitigation & threat model: Defense-in-depth with (1) minimal process privileges, (2) sidecar proxy authn for all outbound flows, (3) strong segmentation between control and data planes, (4) immutable node images and signed model artifacts, and (5) continuous log collection for rapid detection and response.

Attachments included: Redwood_Tenant_Provenance_Controls.pdf (annotated mapping + evidence), Redwood_Network_Topology_v2.svg (diagram), audit_log_sample_202609.csv (masked), egress_flow_examples.txt.

Next steps: please confirm receipt and whether you prefer the NDA route for SOC/penetration artifacts. We're available to walk through the diagrams at 10:00 AM PT Friday if that still works — I will send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Tenant_Provenance_Controls.pdf (pdf), Redwood_Network_Topology_v2.svg (svg), audit_log_sample_202609.csv (csv), egress_flow_examples.txt (txt)
